comparisons.peer_topic: Composition of TLAC and Eligible Debt
comparisons.peer_summary: TLAC includes common and preferred stock and eligible long-term debt issued by Group Inc., defined as unsecured debt with at least one year maturity and other requirements, while external long-term debt consists of eligible debt subject to a haircut if due between one and two years.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Goldman Sachs disclose the composition and definition of their TLAC-eligible debt, specifically noting that eligible long-term debt is defined as unsecured debt with a remaining maturity of at least one year. BAC provides specific outstanding amounts and a callable schedule for these notes, whereas GS defines the structure and mentions external long-term debt adjustments (haircuts) for debt due within one to two years. Both indicate that TLAC eligibility hinges on maturity criteria (at least one year).

sentences.text: At December 31, 2024, Bank of America Corporation's senior notes of $180.3 billion included $167.5 billion of outstanding notes, substantially all of which are both TLAC eligible and callable at least one year before their stated maturities.

Of these senior notes, $22.1 billion will be callable and become TLAC ineligible during 2025, and $21.6 billion, $24.9 billion, $19.5 billion and $8.0 billion will do so during each of 2026 through 2029, respectively, and $71.4 billion thereafter.

• TLAC includes common and preferred stock, and eligible long-term debt issued by Group Inc. Eligible long-term debt represents unsecured debt, which has a remaining maturity of at least one year and satisfies additional requirements.
• External long-term debt consists of eligible long-term debt subject to a haircut if it is due to be paid between one and two years.

comparisons.peer_topic: TLAC and LTD Ratio Definitions and Requirements
comparisons.peer_summary: Required TLAC ratios include applicable buffers and consist of CET1 capital, Additional Tier 1 capital (excluding noncontrolling interests), and eligible LTD, with LTD reduced by 50% for unpaid principal due in one to two years. Clean holding company requirements prohibit covered BHCs from incurring external debt with maturities less than one year and cap certain other external liabilities at 5% of outstanding external TLAC, while capital deductions apply for investments in unsecured debt instruments issued by the Parent Company or other G-SIBs.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and Morgan Stanley disclose the structural requirements for TLAC-eligible debt, specifically emphasizing the one-year maturity threshold. BAC notes that substantially all senior notes are 'callable at least one year before their stated maturities' to remain TLAC-eligible, while MS explicitly states that 'clean holding company requirements' prohibit incurring external debt with an original maturity of less than one year. Both use this one-year constraint to define the boundary between eligible TLAC debt and ineligible short-term liabilities.

sentences.text: At December 31, 2024, Bank of America Corporation's senior notes of $180.3 billion included $167.5 billion of outstanding notes, substantially all of which are both TLAC eligible and callable at least one year before their stated maturities.

Furthermore, under the clean holding company requirements, a covered BHC is prohibited from incurring any external debt with an original maturity of less than one year or certain other liabilities, regardless of whether the liabilities are fully secured or otherwise senior to eligible LTD, or entering into certain other prohibited transactions.
